sentences.text: The concise facts of the case as alleged in the FIR lodged at the instance of the mother of the prosecutrix are that her (2 of 3) [CRLMB-10078/2023] daughter was drugged and thereafter, raped by the petitioner and his friends Hardik Suthar and Jay Suthar in a hotel on 07.06.2023.
She has alleged that the three accused named above also captured photographs and made a video on the basis of which they blackmailed the prosecutrix.

It is further alleged therein that after this incident,
she was again taken to another hotel where she was raped again as well as photographed and video-graphed.

As per the allegations, she was repeatedly blackmailed and made to give gold ornaments as well as cash amounting to Rs. 15,000/- to the accused-persons and she was being pressurized with the threat that her video and photograph would be made public by them.
3. It is contended on behalf of the accused-petitioner that no case for the alleged offences is made out against him/her and his incarceration is not warranted.
There are no factors at play in the case at hand that may work against grant of bail to the accused- petitioner and he has been made an accused based on conjectures and surmises.

It is further contended that the prosecutrix has given a contradictory statement before the trial court and that her statement recorded under Section 164 CrPC goes against the story of the prosecution.

4. Contrary to the submissions of learned counsel for the petitioner, learned Public Prosecutor opposes the bail application and submits that the present case is not fit for enlargement of accused on bail.
5. Have considered the submissions made by both the parties and have perused the material available on record.

The FIR has (3 of 3) [CRLMB-10078/2023] been filed after a delay of more than one month and no such obscene material has been recovered on the strength of which threats could have been made so as to explain the delay in filing of the FIR.

In light of the specific submission that the statements of the prosecutrix are not consistent at different stages of investigation and trial, the plea of consent for the purpose of granting bail at this stage cannot be overlooked.

There are two different documents mentioning two different dates as the date of birth of the prosecutrix, however,
ascertainment of age of the prosecutrix is a question to be decided after appreciation of evidence during trial.
There is high probability that the trial may take long time to conclude.
In light of these facts and circumstances, it is deemed suitable to grant the benefit of bail to the petitioner in the present matter.
Needless to say, none of the observations made herein under shall affect the rights of either of the parties during trial and this Court refrains from commenting on the niceties of the matter.

6. Accordingly, the instant bail application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. is allowed and it is ordered that the accused-petitioner as named in the cause title shall be enlarged on bail provided he furnishes a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- with two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the learned trial Judge for his appearance before the court concerned on all the dates of hearing as and when called upon to do so.

(FARJAND ALI),J 127/-
